messages:
acme_admin: Hi team — our app started failing to call our Redwood Private endpoint through corporate proxy this morning. Calls return "SSL: TLSV1_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE" and 502s from the proxy. curl shows:

acme_admin: curl -v https://private.redwood.local/v1/health --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Finished (20)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, fatal handshake failure (40)
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to private.redwood.local:443

sara_support: Thanks — sorry about that. Can you paste the output of `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.local:443 -servername private.redwood.local -tls1_3 -msg` and also try `-tls1_2`? Also confirm whether your corp proxy does TLS interception (terminates TLS) or allows CONNECT passthrough.

dan_neteng: Quick note: many enterprise proxies enforce a specific cipher suite order and disable curves like X25519. If Redwood presents only TLS1.3/ECDSA-first ciphers the proxy may not be able to negotiate.

acme_admin: We do have TLS inspection enabled (MITM) on the proxy; it substitutes our corp cert. Attached is openssl output (trimmed):

acme_admin: * TLSv1.3 handshake start
acme_admin: * 1:cipher suites: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
acme_admin: * server cert uses ECDSA with curve X25519
acme_admin: * handshake failed: no shared cipher

sara_support: That lines up with a cipher/curve mismatch. Two recommended paths:
1) Ask your proxy team to allow ECDHE curves X25519 and secp256r1 and permit TLS1.3 cipher suites (AES-GCM/CHACHA20) for outbound to the Private endpoint. Or at least add `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256` for TLS1.2 fallback.
2) As a temporary workaround, configure the proxy to use CONNECT passthrough for private.redwood.local so TLS is end-to-end and Redwood's cert is not re-signed.

dan_neteng: For repro steps for your infra team:
- Run: `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.local:443 -servername private.redwood.local -cipher 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' -curves X25519,secp256r1`
- Also test with `-tls1_2` vs `-tls1_3` and capture the exact ClientHello cipher list.
- Collect tcpdump during handshake and share a pcap if safe.

acme_admin: Ran the first test, TLS1.2 + that cipher succeeds. TLS1.3 fails. Proxy team says they only allow a limited TLS1.3 profile (no X25519) and re-sign with RSA certs.

tim_eng: OK — two actions from Redwood side: (A) we can enable RSA-compatible cipher fallback on the Private endpoint so clients with restrictive proxies can negotiate (requires RSA key/cert rotation); (B) we can offer a hosted relay for you to egress to (hosted endpoint that accepts your proxy). I'll open an internal escalation.

daisy_srebot: Escalation created: RINF-2026-487. Assigned to eng-runtime. Please attach openssl logs + proxy TLS profile.

sara_support: For your proxy team, concrete config snippet (F5/Bluecoat style) to allow curves: `tls-profile set named-proxy-profile { tls1-3 enabled; ecdh-curves x25519,secp256r1; cipher-suites TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256; }`

acme_admin: I'll share this with them and follow up. For now, enabling TLS1.2 fallback on Redwood sounds fine if it reduces outages.

tim_eng: We'll evaluate RSA-fallback impact and timeline. If we go that route we'll notify you with a maintenance window. In the meantime, CONNECT passthrough is the fastest fix.

acme_admin: Thanks — will update after proxy change. Appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:

sara_support: Thanks — marking as in-progress until eng confirms RINF-2026-487 resolution.
